evals.name: operator-fixes-and-exponent
evals.prompt: I have a data dictionary that keeps failing to upload. The branching logic has some wrong operators I think. Can you fix it? The file is at evals/files/test_dd_operators.csv
evals.expected_output: Should run fix_dd.py and produce a corrected CSV with a change log: == → = in sex_other and pregnant branching logic, "1" → '1' and && → AND in pregnant, != → <> in bmi, and Identifier? Y → y on pt_name. Should also flag (from its own expression review, not the script) that the BMI formula [weight_kg]/[height_m]^2 needs parentheses around base and exponent: [weight_kg]/(([height_m])^(2)).

assertions.name: Ran fix_dd.py script
assertions.description: The response shows evidence of running the fix_dd.py script (not just manually describing issues)

assertions.name: Fixed == to =
assertions.description: The output CSV or change log shows that == was replaced with = in branching logic

assertions.name: Fixed && to AND
assertions.description: The output CSV or change log shows && was replaced with AND

assertions.name: Fixed != to <>
assertions.description: The output CSV or change log shows != was replaced with <>

assertions.name: Produced a corrected CSV file
assertions.description: A corrected CSV file was written and its path was shared with the user

assertions.name: Normalized Identifier Y flag
assertions.description: Reported the normalization of Identifier?=Y to y (or the output CSV reflects this)

evals.name: structural-errors-and-calctext
evals.prompt: Please fix this data dictionary — I got errors when trying to upload it. File: evals/files/test_dd_structural.csv
evals.expected_output: Should parse the DD, run the fixer, and identify: (1) missing choices on 'diagnosis' (Dropdown) and 'adverse_event' (radio) — flagged, not auto-fixed; (2) double-quoted literals in the @CALCTEXT annotation on pat_name (including "Unnamed" and the empty-string check) — auto-fixed to single quotes; (3) 'Dropdown' field type — lowercased; (4) duplicate record_id — flagged as an error; (5) ae_description has validation min=100/max=2000 with no validation type — worth noting to the user. Should produce a corrected CSV.

assertions.name: Flagged missing choices
assertions.description: Correctly flagged that 'diagnosis' (Dropdown) and 'adverse_event' (radio) have no choices defined

assertions.name: Fixed uppercase field type
assertions.description: Lowercased 'Dropdown' to 'dropdown' in the output

assertions.name: Flagged duplicate variable name
assertions.description: Identified that record_id appears twice and flagged it as an error

assertions.name: Fixed double quotes in @CALCTEXT
assertions.description: Converted double quotes to single quotes inside the @CALCTEXT annotation on pat_name

assertions.name: Produced a corrected CSV file
assertions.description: A corrected CSV file was written and its path was shared with the user

assertions.name: Provided clear summary of fixes and remaining issues
assertions.description: The response clearly separates what was auto-fixed from what still requires manual action

evals.name: mixed-whitespace-and-missing-formulas
evals.prompt: My data dictionary has a bunch of issues — whitespace in variable names, wrong operators, missing choices, missing formulas. Can you fix what you can and tell me what's left? File is at evals/files/test_dd_mixed.csv
evals.expected_output: Should parse and run the fixer. Should fix: (1) whitespace around ' mrn '; (2) == → = in fu_date and fu_notes branching logic, != → <> in fu_notes; (3) YES → y in Required Field? for dob; (4) validation min/max cleared on the phq9_total calc field. Should flag: (5) missing choices on refer_source, smoking, and alcohol; (6) missing formula on phq9_total. phq9_q1/phq9_q2 are radio fields in matrix group 'phq9' sharing identical choices — that is a valid matrix and should not be flagged. Should deliver a corrected CSV.

assertions.name: Fixed whitespace in variable name
assertions.description: Stripped leading/trailing whitespace from ' mrn ' variable name

assertions.name: Fixed == and != operators in branching logic
assertions.description: Converted == to = and != to <> in fu_date and fu_notes branching logic

assertions.name: Normalized YES to y in Required Field
assertions.description: Converted YES → y in the Required Field? column for dob

assertions.name: Flagged fields with missing choices
assertions.description: Flagged refer_source, smoking, and alcohol as missing choices

assertions.name: Flagged calc field with no formula
assertions.description: Flagged phq9_total as a calc field with no formula

assertions.name: Produced a corrected CSV file
assertions.description: A corrected CSV file was written and its path was shared with the user

assertions.name: Cleared min/max on calc field
assertions.description: Cleared Text Validation Min/Max (0/27) on the phq9_total calc field

evals.name: apostrophe-in-double-quoted-string
evals.prompt: Can you clean up the branching logic and calc text in this DD before I upload it? evals/files/test_dd_apostrophe.csv
evals.expected_output: Should run fix_dd.py. In city_note, "New Haven"/"Hamden" become single-quoted, == → =, || → OR. In obrien_note, == → = but "O'Brien" must stay double-quoted (NOT 'O'Brien', which would break the expression) and be reported as a warning. In the greeting @CALCTEXT (nested if), "Dia duit", "Hamden", "Hi", "Hello" become single-quoted while "O'Brien" stays double-quoted, and the closing parentheses are intact.

assertions.name: Kept "O'Brien" double-quoted
assertions.description: The output CSV still contains "O'Brien" in double quotes in obrien_note branching logic and in the greeting annotation; it never contains 'O'Brien'

assertions.name: Converted safe literals
assertions.description: "New Haven" and "Hamden" in city_note are now single-quoted, with == → = and || → OR

assertions.name: Handled nested @CALCTEXT
assertions.description: All safe literals in the nested if() of the greeting @CALCTEXT were converted (including those after the inner if), and the expression is otherwise unchanged

assertions.name: Reported the kept literal
assertions.description: Told the user that "O'Brien" was left double-quoted and why

evals.name: mixed-case-variable-names-referenced
evals.prompt: REDCap says my variable names are invalid. Fix this DD please: evals/files/test_dd_mixedcase.csv
evals.expected_output: Should run fix_dd.py, which must NOT rename Age or Smoker. Should report both as uppercase-variable errors listing where they are referenced ([Age] in Smoker branching logic, age_months formula, age_text @CALCTEXT; [Smoker] in packs_day branching logic). Should ask the user to confirm before renaming, warn that renaming orphans any collected data, and — only if the user agrees — rename consistently (age/smoker) everywhere, including every reference.

assertions.name: Did not silently rename
assertions.description: The corrected CSV produced before user confirmation still has Age and Smoker, with references unchanged — no half-renamed file where the variable is 'age' but logic still says [Age]

assertions.name: Listed references
assertions.description: Reported the rows/fields that reference [Age] and [Smoker]

assertions.name: Asked before renaming
assertions.description: Asked the user to confirm the rename and mentioned the data-loss risk if data has been collected
